_comment: Source of truth for the app's feature inventory and its test coverage. Humans edit this when adding/removing a feature. CI (scripts/check-feature-manifest.mjs) fails when code drifts from this file (new/removed endpoints, components, or dead test references) and regenerates the auto block in docs/APP-STATE.md. Tiers follow risk-based testing: critical = smoke-gated on every PR; important = regression suite; nice = best-effort; internal = tooling, not user-facing.

tiers.critical: Core user journey. If it breaks the app is unusable. Must have a behavioral smoke test gated on every PR.
tiers.important: Real user value, frequent use. Must have regression coverage.
tiers.nice: Enhancement or easter egg. Best-effort coverage.
tiers.internal: Tooling / ops. Not part of the user-facing product.

coverageLegend.behavioral: A test actually executes the feature's logic and asserts real behavior.
coverageLegend.mocked: Tested through e2e/unit but the failure-prone layer is mocked away (e.g. silent audio).
coverageLegend.source-only: Only verified by grepping source text (makeover-*.test.js); regressions that keep the same tokens pass.
coverageLegend.device-only: Cannot run in Chromium-on-Linux CI; needs real Safari/iOS or a real device.

features.name: Poem categorization / Explore
features.userFacing: Account menu -> Explore Poems: filter/browse poems by mood, topic, motif, cross-dimension family, emotional intensity, and 0-10 reading difficulty; tap a result to expand the full poem in place.
features.gap: server.test.js covers the enabled/disabled API paths with a mocked pool; no e2e yet for the Explore Poems UI (filter chips, in-place poem expand).

features.name: Onboarding preference flow (6 steps)
features.userFacing: Full-screen six-step flow at /onboarding: a welcome that offers a curated feed or a way straight into the reading, then mood, imagery (motif, optional), family, reading difficulty and era. Every option and bilingual label is read from the live categorization API, and the era and difficulty bands are cut from the LIVE DISTRIBUTION (GET /api/categories -> distributions) rather than hardcoded. NO poem counts are shown anywhere: the answers are a weight on the feed and never a filter (see feed-preference-weighting), so a number beside an option describes a narrowing that does not happen, and printing one on all six steps turned six different questions into six readings of the same table. Dropping them also removed the per-step cascading scope refetch, so the flow no longer issues a request per answer; the counts still exist on the API and the draw inspector still reports them after a draw, where they mean something. Each step is its own component with its own design feature rather than one data-driven picker reskinned six times: mood is a field of coloured embers that washes the background with the mix of what you pick; imagery is a grid of line-art glyphs, because the question is about images; family is a shelf of vertical spines you pull one volume out of; reading difficulty is a type specimen, each band set in a progressively more classical face (Fustat, Amiri, Katibeh) so the letterforms demonstrate the answer; era hangs its bands off a timeline rail headed by their real century ranges. Every step is skippable and single-select steps toggle off when the chosen option is tapped again. Leaving from the welcome screen writes no completedAt, so declining is not recorded as a finished answer. Answers save to localStorage.onboardingPrefs (shape unchanged: family, moods, motifs, era, difficulty). The account menu is the way back in: an entry that reads 'Set up your feed' with no saved answers and 'Change your feed' once there are some, because finishing the flow REPLACES them. No confirm step — the flow seeds every picker from the saved answers and writes nothing until the last one, so backing out early leaves them intact. PreferencesDrawer was built to re-edit them and still uses the older generic PreferenceStep, and is mounted nowhere. Signed in, the answers also mirror to user_settings.onboarding_preferences (versioned JSONB) so they follow the reader across devices; on sign-in the two sides are reconciled whole by most-recent completedAt, and a payload whose version this build does not recognise is left untouched on both sides.
features.gap: Unit tests cover band derivation against a real measured histogram (era grouping, NULL-century handling, quantile difficulty cuts), the categoryTags adapter, stepping all six steps to completion in order, the welcome exit writing no completedAt, mood ordering by feeling rather than corpus size, the optional motif step, single-select clearing on a second tap, the absence of any digit on an option or its aria-label, and the empty pre-migration state. Cross-device sync is unit-tested in both merge directions, plus write-through, read-back and version mismatch, against a stubbed Supabase client. No e2e yet for the rendered flow, nothing exercises the JSONB column against a real Postgres row, and nothing automated checks the layout at phone width -- the six steps were verified by hand at 393x852 and 375x812.

Not yet mounted on a route - the two editor surfaces are read-only because the categorization API exposes no writes (see their TODO(write-api) blocks).

features.name: Preference-scored feed selection
features.userFacing: Onboarding answers bias which poem the feed serves next WITHOUT filtering the corpus. Every candidate is SCORED 0-5 on how much of the answer set it satisfies (family 0.8, mood 1.2, motif 1.0, era 1.0, difficulty 1.0), and one is sampled from that score by a softmax whose temperature loosens over 30 poems seen. Family is weighted below the dimensions it is built out of, and discounted further when the only value carrying the family match is one the reader already named as a mood or motif, so the two correlated answers cannot outvote the three independent ones. Multi-select steps give partial credit: matching two of three chosen moods beats one of three, without punishing a reader for picking more. Era and difficulty give graded credit to near misses (an adjacent century, an accessibility score just outside the band) rather than cutting at the band edge; undated (late/modern) poems stay eligible under a dated band at reduced credit, so picking one period over another visibly changes the feed. Candidates come from two pages: one ANCHORED on the reader's broadest single answer, and one wholly UNANCHORED, which is what keeps every poem in the library reachable on every draw. Replaces the earlier core/adjacent/wild pool mix, which had no gradation between matching five answers and matching one. On a strong match the reader sees a quiet 'chosen for <label>' line; on a weak one, deliberately nothing. The inspector's collapsed CLASSIFIER'S RATIONALE now reads bilingual like every chip above it: Arabic in Amiri, English under it in mono. Both languages come from one field, categories.rationale_en - written by the classifier under prompt version distill-2, or back-filled on demand for older rows by POST /api/poems/:id/rationale-translation, which translates server-side and PERSISTS into the poem row so only the first reader to expand it ever pays. It fires on expand only, never across the feed, and with no backend GEMINI_API_KEY (or offline, or on an upstream failure) it resolves to nothing and the Arabic stands alone - no spinner, no error line. The answers now shape the WHOLE feed, not just its first slide: completing the flow (or editing the answers, or signing in to an account whose answers win the merge) redraws the feed from slot 0, every slide is its own scored draw out of one shared candidate pool, and infinite scroll keeps drawing by score instead of falling back to random. Slides 0 and 1 are taken by RANK rather than sampled, so the two poems a reader sees immediately after answering are the best available match rather than a lucky one; temperature governs slide 2 onward, which is what keeps every poem reachable. The ranked opening is opt-in per draw rather than implied by starting near slot 0, so an ordinary mid-feed refill cannot re-run it, and the redraw claims the deferred auto-load so nothing fetches a replacement poem and moves the reader off slide 0.
features.gap: Unit tests pin the weighting and every partial-credit rule, the family/mood overlap discount in both directions, both halves of the no-lock-in guarantee (a zero-scoring candidate keeps a strictly positive softmax weight, AND the unanchored candidate page exists so it can be a candidate at all), the temperature calibration that carries the old wild 0.15 -> 0.25 mix forward, the batched multi-slide draw (ranked opening, sampled tail, no repeats, stable tie-break, load-more does not re-rank), the per-poem draw records the inspector reads, and the preference change notification that triggers the redraw. They also pin what the inspector RENDERS, so the panel cannot become a second implementation of the weighting: the per-term score decomposition sums to the score the scorer returned, and the per-dimension explanation resolves each facet to one of matched / present-but-unasked / asked-for-but-absent / partial, including the asked-for-but-absent case that the old truncating table had no way to express at all. The integration in fetchPoem.js (two-page candidate fetch, dedup, fallback to a plain fetch on an empty result) has no dedicated tests yet, and the inspector's LAYOUT (that nothing in the why block truncates at 375px) is verified in a browser rather than in CI; the end-to-end redraw is verified in a browser, not in CI. The browser check asserts a COUNT (exactly one scored draw fires) and that the reader rests on slot 0 ranked, because the regression it caught passed every non-zero check: the ranked opening was drawn correctly and then clobbered by a second fetch before the reader saw it. The rationale back-fill is unit-tested on both sides: the route is pinned on the cached path (no model call, no second write), the jsonb_set merge and its write-once guard, and the 503/502/no_rationale branches; the client service is pinned on POSTing to the persisting route, de-duplicating concurrent expands, and resolving null for every failure. The rendered bilingual block at 375px is verified in a browser, not in CI.
